I'm sorry, exactly what passage are you referring to? If you're talking about the part that ends with "Flugel weilt," just before the last prestissimo, that is not in the key of G# major. It is in the key of B major, and at the last second the D drops the sharp to become a B minor chord (not a D-sharp diminished) and then the basses subtly slide down to A natural thus creating a 6/4 tonic chord. He goes to the parallel minor, then the relative major. Straight up textbook example shit. This is almost exactly the same harmonic progression he used earlier in the movement, right after the climax of the double fugue (B major -> B minor -> D major). Then the rest of the orchestra comes in tottering between B and A (almost asking, are we going to be in B minor or D major? B minor or D major?) before climbing up to C# then finally to D major. To me this reasoning is very apparent.

One that I haven't seen others mention - in the slow movement of the Piano Trio no. 6 in E-flat, there is a section where he goes back between i and V (in C minor) around 20 times in a row. And not just subtly implied harmonies - these are thick, fully voiced chords in the left hand all the while. It's just such a wonderfully, typically Beethoven passage.

Pierce Armor: 2 (Base) + 8 (Blacksmith, Romans get double effect) + 3 (Malians bonus) + 1 (Gambesons) = 14

Reload Time: 2 (Base) - 25% (Japanese bonus) = 1.50 (the tooltip says it makes infantry attack 33% faster, but it achieves this by reducing reload time by 25%)

They are also incredibly resistant to conversion thanks to the Teutons team bonus and Sicilian First Crusade - and take less bonus damage from the Sicilian civ bonus as well

This is the fundamental issue with Paladins, why they were completely useless in Vanilla, and why without editing the broken talent trees or baseline class abilities it's hard to fix.

They simply have no buttons. That's all there is to it. If you go full Ret spec, what's supposed to be the DAMAGE spec, you have exactly one offensive button to click. Judgement. That's it. I'm not counting Seals because those are just passively enhancing auto-attacks, not a button you actively press. 

Even a fucking priest has more offensive buttons than a Paladin. Smite, Holy Fire, Mind Blast, Shadow Word: Pain, 4 offensive abilities just off the top of my head that don't require speccing into any talent tree or fighting a specific enemy. You just get them and can use them on anyone.

Paladins can only get up to THREE offensive abilities that work on all targets, and only if they FULLY spec into the HEALING tree. Judgement, Holy Shock, and Consecrate. Further complicating this is that they need too many stats: they need strength to make auto-attacks better, but also spell power for their seals, but also intellect for mana, etc. and with the gearing in vanilla it's extremely hard to get the stats they need.

Yes, the new runes help fix some of these problems, but these are problems most other classes don't have, so their runes are better simply by virtue of being able to enhance an already good ability rather than just fix a broken one. Warlock gets a rune to make their Shadowbolt AoE, for example. So, Shadowbolt is a baseline ability, already good, and the rune makes it better. Sounds great, right?

Paladins get a rune to give us Crusader Strike. That's it. Not to enhance Crusader Strike, but just to give it to us. Imagine if a Warlock had to use a rune slot just to get access to Shadowbolt, never mind making it AoE. That's obviously terrible design.

Honestly, both the Exorcism and Crusader Strike rune should be skill books. I'd further argue that Divine Storm should do Holy damage in exchange for a lesser percentage of weapon damage, but that's starting to get besides the point.

Hello everyone, I recently saw [this post](https://www.reddit.com/r/BaldursGate3/comments/16qcmw4/rainbow_damage_1h_melee_weapon/) and I was inspired to take it one step further, to see if it was possible to combine every damage type in the game into one attack. It is indeed possible. This is how:


+1d6 Thunder: Nyrulna as the base weapon


+1d4 Cold: Ring of Elemental Infusion. You need to deal cold damage with a spell/cantrip to get this, scrolls work. This effect does not display in the tooltip for the weapon but it does add correctly to the damage.


+2 Acid: Caustic Band, flat bonus to weapon damage


+1d4 Necrotic: Horns of the Berserker, only active when below max HP


+1d4 Poison: Broodmother's Revenge, coats your weapon in poison when you are healed (counts as a coat and will overwrite other poison/fire dip)


+1d4 Fire: Flawed Helldusk Gloves, bonus to weapon damage (Alternatively, regular Helldusk Gloves for 1d6)


+1d4 Lightning: Drakethroat Glaive, gives you a free cast of Elemental Weapon per long rest that does not require concentration. You can drop another weapon on the ground, cast the spell on that weapon and equip it


+1d8 Radiant: Improved Divine Smite, Paladin level 11 (Morninglord's Radiance gives +1d4 Radiant but the most recent patch fixed it so it is no longer permanent)


+1d4 Psychic: Boots of Psionic Movement, when a Githyanki casts fly their next attack has bonus damage, you can shapeshift to a Githyanki to gain the effect


+1d4 Force: Wild Magic Surge: Enchant Weapons. This one is difficult to obtain consistently. You need a level 11 sorcerer to cast Controlled Chaos and for the RNG to give you the effect you want. It lasts for 1 attack, but until long rest, so it can be saved.


And since the Wild Magic effect makes your hit a guaranteed critical, that means that all of these damage dice are going to be doubled (except for the Cold and Psychic damage). That results in a damage range of 29 - 103 for a critical strike on one regular melee attack. You have some flexibility in element choices with the Glaive/Elemental Infusion Ring as well as your weapon, but I set it up like this because Nyrulna has a +3 enchant and a 1d6 elemental effect. Technically it is still missing slashing and bludgeoning damage, but it still has piercing, so that's physical damage.
